children: Global media and entertainment company iHeartMedia
will be reporting earnings this Monday after market close. Here’s what you need to know.

iHeartMedia beat analysts’ revenue expectations last quarter, reporting revenues of $977.2 million, up 4.7% year on year. It was a slower quarter for the company, with a significant miss of analysts’ EPS estimates.
Is iHeartMedia a buy or sell going into earnings?

params.linkText: Read our full analysis here, it’s free for active Edge members

children: This quarter, the market is expecting iHeartMedia’s revenue to grow 5.6% year on year, a reversal from the 1.1% decrease it recorded in the same quarter last year.

Analysts covering the company have generally reconfirmed their estimates over the last 30 days, suggesting they anticipate the business will stay the course heading into earnings. iHeartMedia rarely misses Wall Street’s revenue estimates.

Looking at iHeartMedia’s peers in the consumer discretionary - broadcasting segment, some have already reported their Q3 results, giving us a hint as to what we can expect. FOX delivered year-on-year revenue growth of 22.3%, beating analysts’ expectations by 6.5%, and E.W. Scripps reported revenues up 3.6%, falling short of estimates by 0.5%. FOX traded up 6.1% following the results while E.W. Scripps was also up 8.5%.

There has been positive sentiment among investors in the consumer discretionary - broadcasting segment, with share prices up 4.7% on average over the last month. iHeartMedia is down 8.1% during the same time and is heading into earnings with an average analyst price target of $3.63 (compared to the current share price of $1.77).
